subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw create a first-class per-skill writable data directory contract, and should that contract be filesystem-based, plugin/SQLite-backed, or ClawHub authoring guidance only?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the right owner for skill runtime data affects public metadata, persistent storage, sandbox visibility, backup behavior, and third-party skill authoring rules.

options.title: Define a core skill data contract
options.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned convention or helper for per-skill data and require docs/tests around install, runtime, and sandbox behavior.

options.title: Keep it as ClawHub authoring guidance
options.body: Document that skill packages should self-contain or choose their own data location without adding new core metadata or runtime behavior.

options.title: Defer to plugin state APIs
options.body: Avoid filesystem directories and route durable skill-owned data through plugin KV or SQLite-backed extension APIs if skills need state.

recommendation.title: Define a core skill data contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned convention or helper for per-skill data and require docs/tests around install, runtime, and sandbox behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is recent work across skill lifecycle/docs plus the product boundary between core, ClawHub, and plugin APIs.
